usual_baseline: Core identifiers are usually good (name 99% [1337]) but clinical content is poor. Outstanding tasks 31–38% [1226, 1308], blood results 19–29% [1226, 1308], presenting complaint missing in 78% [1303], whom to contact 0% [1417], laterality 22% [1494]. Overall data handed over 72.6% [1226]; complete trauma meeting presentations 24.0% [1554].
fix_that_works: A structured proforma, best electronic. Overall handover data 72.6% to 93.2% [1226]. Electronic proforma: all but one item at 95% or more, uptake 100% [1308]. Electronic ward round notes: core items 100% [1417]. EPR trauma meeting proforma: clear plan 63% to 98% [1494]. Template for presentations: complete 24.0% to 81.3% [1554]. PTWR proforma: consultant unidentifiable 19% to 4% [1303].
fix_that_fails: Items without their own field stay poor. Blood results 19% to 20% [1226]. Whom to contact 0% to 14.70% on electronic notes [1417]. TTO fell to 5% and was dropped [1337]. Weekend proforma completion stayed poor [1303]. Theatre checklist completed in 11% [1494]. Pending investigations 82% even on the electronic form [1308].
consultant_advice: Heavily done. Every audit finds gaps and a proforma closes most of them. Don't repeat it. Audit whether the proforma is still used a year on with new doctors [1337, 1494], weekend handover, or whether handover gaps link to missed tasks or harm.
